akhfash:1-1.t: He said ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٍ﴾: "تبّت" is jussive (majzūm), because when the feminine tāʾ is in the verb it is jussive, as in "ضَرَبَ" and "ضَرَبْتُ"*. As for His words ﴿وتّب﴾, it has fatḥa because it is a masculine past verb. «[Translator's note: by "jussive" (jazm) the author means that the final letter carries sukūn.]»

akhfash:4-4.t: And He said ﴿وَٱمْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ ٱلْحَطَبِ﴾: He means "and his wife, the carrier of firewood, will burn" (وَتَصْلَى امرأتُه حمالةِ الحَطَب), and ﴿حمالةُ الحَطَبِ﴾ is a description of her. Some made ﴿حمّالةَ الحَطَب﴾ accusative as dispraise (dhamm), as if He said "I mention her, the carrier of firewood" (ذكرتُها حمالةَ الحطبِ). It is also permissible for ﴿حمالةَ الحطبِ﴾ to be indefinite, with tanwīn intended, so that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of "امرأته", made accusative by His words ﴿تَصْلى﴾. «[Translator's note: «حمالةِ» in the first paraphrase is so vowelled in the source.]»

celaleyn:1-1.t: When the Prophet ﷺ called his people and said, "I am a warner to you before a severe punishment," his uncle Abū Lahab said, "Perish you! Is it for this that you called us?" So there was revealed: ﴿تَبَّتْ﴾: lost ﴿يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ﴾, that is, his whole self; it is expressed by "the two hands" figuratively (majāzan), because most actions are carried out with them. This clause is an imprecation (duʿāʾ).

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَتَبَّ﴾: he lost. This is a statement of fact (khabar), like their saying "May Allah destroy him — and he has been destroyed." When the Prophet ﷺ warned him of the punishment, he said, "If what my nephew says is true, I will ransom myself from it with my wealth and my children," so there was revealed: ﴿مَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ﴾, that is, and his earning, that is, his children. «ما أغنى» is in the sense of «يغني» ("will avail").

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿سَيَصْلَى نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ﴾, that is, of flaming and blazing; so it is what his kunya (agnomen) comes to, [the kunya having been given him] because of the flaming of his face in radiance and redness.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَامْرَأَتُهُ﴾: conjoined to the pronoun of «يصلى», which is permitted by the separation by the object and its ṣifa (adjective). She is Umm Jamīl. ﴿حَمَّالَةُ﴾ — with the nominative and with the accusative [حَمَّالَةَ] — ﴿الْحَطَبِ﴾: thorns and saʿdān [a thorny plant], which she would throw in the path of the Prophet ﷺ.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فِي جِيدِهَا﴾: her neck ﴿حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ﴾, that is, of palm fibre. This clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «حمالة الحطب», which is a naʿt (adjective) of «امرأته», or the khabar (predicate) of an implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ (subject).

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿تَبَّتْ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿يَدا﴾ fāʿil (agent), in the nominative (marfūʿ) with the alif because it is dual. ﴿أَبِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَهَبٍ﴾ also muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَتَبَّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿أَغْنى﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مالُهُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾ a relative noun, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ماله. ﴿كَسَبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿سَيَصْلى﴾ the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿ناراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ذاتَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of نارا. ﴿لَهَبٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَامْرَأَتُهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle (ḥarf istiʾnāf), and mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حَمَّالَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «أذم حمالة» (I censure the carrier). ﴿الْحَطَبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿فِي جِيدِها﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿حَبْلٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ مَسَدٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of حبل; the clause «امرأته..» is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position. The verbal clause ﴿أذم حمالة الحطب﴾ is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa), with no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَبَّتْ): it perished/lost. al-Zamakhsharī said: "al-tabāb is destruction, and from it their saying:
أشابة أم تابة أي هالكة من الهرم والتعجيز
(Is she a young woman or a perishing one, i.e. perishing from old age and infirmity?)
and the meaning is: his hands perished, because, as is reported, he took up a stone to throw at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The wording of Ibn Khālawayh: "Its meaning is 'his hands lost'. The maṣdar is tabba, yatibbu, tabban, so he is tābb and the object is matbūb, and the imperative is tibba, or if you wish you may write it with kasra, and for a woman tibbī; and 'tabban' and 'atbibna'; when the doubling is lifted the first of the verb is made quiescent, so you bring a connecting alif. A woman is called tābba, i.e. an old woman whose youth has perished. al-Tabāb is destruction; Allah said: 'And the plot of Pharaoh was only in destruction (tabāb)'. ʿAdī said:
اذهبي إنّ كل دنيا ضلال ... والأمانيّ عقرها للتباب لا يروقنك صائر لفناه ... كل دنيا مصيرها للتراب
(Go on, every worldly life is error, and desires, their end is destruction; let not anything bound for annihilation delight you, every worldly life ends in dust.)
And Jarīr said:
عرادة من بقية قوم لوط ... ألا تبّا لما عملوا تبابا
(ʿArrāda is of the remnant of the people of Lūṭ; lo, destruction for what they did, destruction!)
And Kaʿb ibn Mālik said, praising the Prophet ﷺ:
الحق منطقه والعدل سيرته ... فمن يعنه عليه ينج من تبب
(Truth is his speech and justice his conduct; whoever helps him in it is saved from destruction.)
The second tāʾ is the feminine tāʾ because the hand is feminine; and the meaning of 'his hands perished' is 'he perished', because the Arabs attribute strength, power and deeds to the two hands, since it is by them that all deeds take place."
(سَيَصْلى): i.e. he will burn in it; ṣaliya is of the pattern taʿiba. The wording of Ibn Khālawayh is good, and it is: "It is said ṣalaytu the sheep when I roasted it, so I am ṣālin and the sheep is muṣliyya; and from this is the ḥadīth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that a roasted sheep (shāt muṣliyya) was given to him as a gift. al-Farrāʾ allowed shāt muṣlāt because you also say aṣlaytuhā. Roast meat is called al-ṣalāʾ, al-muḍahhab, al-rishrāsh, al-rawdhaq, al-mushannat, al-marmūḍ, al-ramīḍ, al-maḥnūdh, al-ḥanīdh, al-suwayd or al-shuwayd, al-maḥsūs, al-muḥāsh, al-saḥsāḥ, al-anīḍ, al-mufallas and al-mukhaddaʿ, all of which mean roast meat."
(جِيدِها): al-jīd is the neck, its plural ajyād; and al-jayad with fatḥa on the yāʾ is length of neck.
(مَسَدٍ): al-masad is what is twisted tightly of ropes, whether of palm fibre, hide or other. In al-Qāmūs: "al-masad with sukūn on the sīn is a maṣdar meaning twisting; with fatḥa it is the iron axle, or a rope of fibre, or any rope firmly twisted; the plural is masād and amsād. It is said masada ḥablahu yamsuduhu masdan, of the pattern naṣara, i.e. he twisted it well."

* I'rab:
(تَبَّتْ يَدا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ) تبت is a past verb and the tāʾ is for the feminine; يدا أبي لهب is the fāʿil; and تب is conjoined to تبت, i.e. "and that happened and came about", as in his words:
جزاني جزاه الله شرّ جزائه ... جزاء الكلاب العاويات وقد فعل
(He repaid me, may Allah repay him with the worst of repayments, the repayment of howling dogs, and he has done it.)
The clause is optative (duʿāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. It is related in the Ṣaḥīḥayn and elsewhere, the wording being Muslim's, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When "And warn your closest kinsmen" was sent down, the Prophet ﷺ went out until he climbed al-Ṣafā and called out "Yā ṣabāḥāh!" They said: Who is this who calls? They said: Muḥammad. So they gathered to him, and he said: "O Banū so-and-so, O Banū ʿAbd Manāf, O Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib!" They gathered to him and he said: "Do you see: if I told you that horsemen were emerging at the foot of the mountain, would you believe me?" They said: We have never tried you in a lie. He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abū Lahab said: "Perdition to you! Did you gather us only for this?" Then he stood up, and the surah was sent down. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why did He use his kunya, when a kunya is an honour? I say: there are three aspects. The first is that he was famous by the kunya rather than the name, for a man may be known by one or the other, and for that reason the kunya is made to follow the name and the name the kunya as ʿaṭf bayān; so when it was intended to make him notorious by an evil supplication and that it remain a mark upon him, He mentioned the better known of his two designations. This is supported by the reading of one who read يدا أبو لهب, as it is said ʿAlī ibn Abū Ṭālib and Muʿāwiya ibn Abū Sufyān, so that nothing of it is altered and the listener is not confused" — up to where he says: "The second is that his name was ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, so He turned from it to his kunya. The third is that since he was of the people of the Fire and his destination is a fire possessed of flame, his state agreed with his kunya, so he was fit to be mentioned by it, as Abū l-Sharr is said of the wicked and Abū l-Khayr of the good, and as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave Abū l-Muhallab the kunya Abū Ṣufra because of a yellowness (ṣufra) in his face. It was also said that he was given the kunya for the flaming (talahhub) and glow of his cheeks, so it may be mentioned in mockery of him and of his boasting of that." (ما أَغْنى عَنْهُ مالُهُ وَما كَسَبَ) ما may be negative or interrogative; in the second case it is accusative in position through what follows it, the implied form being "what thing did wealth avail him?". Strangely, Ibn Khālawayh parsed it as nominative, as a mubtadaʾ. عنه is attached to أغنى, and ماله is the fāʿil. The wāw is a conjunction; and ما may be maṣdariyya or a relative meaning "his earning" or "what he earned"; it may also be interrogative, accusative in position through what follows it, i.e. "what thing did he earn?". The wording of Ibn Hishām: "The first ما may be negative, i.e. 'it did not avail', or interrogative, in which case it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, the implied form being 'what avail did his wealth avail him?'; its being a mubtadaʾ is weak." (سَيَصْلى ناراً ذاتَ لَهَبٍ) The sīn is a particle of futurity; يصلى is an imperfect verb and its agent is "he", i.e. Abū Lahab; نارا is the mafʿūl bihi, and ذات لهب is a naʿt of نارا, because it is the destination of his kunya and its resort. (وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ فِي جِيدِها حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ) وامرأته is conjoined to the pronoun in يصلى, which is allowed by the separation by the object and its adjective; she is Umm Jamīl, the sister of Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb; she was one-eyed and died strangled by her rope. They said:
"She used to carry a bundle of thorns, caltrops and saʿdān and scatter it at night in the path of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It was also said that she went about with slander; one who goes about with slanders, who sows discord between people, is said to carry firewood among them, i.e. he kindles the flame between them and stirs up evil. He said:
من البيض لم تصطد على ظهر لأمة ... ولم تمش بين الحي بالحطب الرطب
(Of the fair ones, who did not hunt upon the back of a coat of mail, and did not walk among the tribe with wet firewood.)
He made the firewood wet to indicate the smoke, which adds to the evil. حمّالة الحطب was read in the accusative as vilification (shatm). al-Zamakhsharī said: 'I prefer this reading.' It was read in the nominative as an adjective of امرأته, which is permitted because the annexation is real, since the past is meant; or as a badal, because it resembles inert nouns through the pure annexation; or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. Ibn Khālawayh said: 'In the codex of Ibn Masʿūd it is murayyaʾatuhu, in diminutive; and the Arabs say hādhihi marʾatī and imraʾatī and zawjī and zawjatī and ḥannatī and ṭillatī and shāʿatī and izārī and maḥall izārī and faḍlatī and ḥarthī. The poet said:
إذا أكل الجراد حروث قوم ... فحرثي همّه أكل الجراد
(When locusts eat the crops of a people, my crop is what the eating of the locusts concerns.)
A woman is also called bayt, and the Arabs allude to a woman by the pearl, the egg, the tall tree, the tamarisk, the palm, the sheep, the cow, the ewe, the shell, the bag, the glass vessels, the fold, the bedding, the sweet basil, the gazelle, the doll (that is, the image), the sandal, the collar, the cloak, the female neighbour, the muzakhkha and the qawmadda. al-Farazdaq alluded to a woman by the scabbard, making her a scabbard for his weapon; she had died pregnant, and he said:
وجفن سلاح قد رزئت ولم أنح ... عليه ولم أبعث عليه البواكيا
وفي جوفه من دارم ذو حفيظة ... لو أن المنايا أنسأته لياليا
(A weapon's scabbard I have lost and did not lament it, nor did I send women to weep over it; and in its belly was a Dārimī of fierce loyalty, had death delayed him some nights.)
Another alluded to her by the place of the saddle on the horse, saying to his wife:
فإما زال سرج عن معدّ ... فأجدر بالحوادث أن تكونا
(If the saddle slips from Maʿadd, it is most likely that events will occur.)
He says: perhaps I shall die and fall away from you, so see how you will be after me.'" في جيدها is a fronted khabar, حبل a postponed mubtadaʾ, and من مسد a naʿt of حبل.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «في جيدها حبل من مسد» there is the art of mockery (tahakkum), mentioned before: He depicted her with a depiction of utmost baseness and lowliness. The meaning of "in her neck is a rope of palm fibre" is: of ropes, and that she carries that bundle and ties it about her neck, to debase her state and portray her in the image of one of the woodgatherers among the servants (mawāhin, plural of māhin, a servant), so that she and her husband would be vexed by it, though they were in a house of might and honour and a position of wealth and standing. Poets have taken hold of the hems of this mockery: one of them taunted al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās, or Ibn ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab, with the "carrier of firewood", and he [the other] said:
ماذا أردت إلى شتمي ومنقصتي ... أم ما تعير من حمّالة الحطب
غراء شادخة في المجد عزّتها ... كانت سليلة شيخ ثاقب الحسب
(What did you intend by insulting me and belittling me? Or what do you reproach in the carrier of firewood? A radiant, far-spreading one whose might in glory was such that she was the offspring of an elder of piercing lineage.)
al-gharrāʾ is the white one; al-shādikha is the widespread, and that is a figure for prominence and elevated rank; al-salīla is one drawn out (sulla) from another; and by "the elder" is meant her father Ḥarb, since she is Umm Jamīl, the sister of Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb. It was said that the carrying of firewood is literal, and it was said that it is figurative, for stirring up strife, because she was a slanderer. And إلى شتمي is attached to something omitted, or to أردت by way of inclusion (tadmīn), i.e. "what thing did you intend, inclining to my insult, or adding it to my insult?", or "what did you want from insulting me, or together with insulting me; did you want to show that you are noble and without flaw?" It is possible that إلى means "from", as the grammarians said, and possible that it is for accompaniment, as they also said regarding His words: "And do not consume their wealth along with (ilā) your wealth." And تعير is originally تتعير, one of the two tāʾs being dropped from it.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٍ﴾.
They mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ stood on al-Marwa and said: O family of Ghālib! And they gathered to him. Then he said: O family of Luʾayy! And the descendants of Ghālib other than Luʾayy went away. Then he kept saying that until he came to Quṣayy.
Abū Lahab said: Here is Quṣayy, come to you; what do you have for them? He said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, has commanded me to warn my nearest kinsfolk, and I have conveyed [it] to you. Abū Lahab said: Did you call us only for this? Ruin to you! So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "وقد تب" (and he has perished). So the first is an imprecation and the second is a statement. Al-Farrāʾ said: "تب" means: lost; as you say to a man: أهلكك الله، وقد أهلكك (May Allah destroy you — and He has destroyed you), or you say: جعلك الله صالحا، وقد جعلك (May Allah make you righteous — and He has made you so).

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱمْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ ٱلْحَطَبِ﴾. «الحمّالة» is read in the nominative and in the accusative. Whoever puts it in the nominative does so in two ways. He says: he will roast in the fire of Hell, he and his wife, حمالةُ الحطب, making it one of her naʿt (adjective). The other nominative is: وامرأتُه حمالةُ الحطب, meaning: and his wife is the carrier of firewood in the Fire; then «فى جيدها» is what makes it nominative. Or if you wish, you make it nominative by «الحمالة», as though you said: ما أغنى عنه ماله، وامرأته هكذا (his wealth did not avail him, and his wife is thus).
As for the accusative, it is in two ways. One of them [151/a] is that you make «الحمالة» a qaṭʿ (cut-off), because it is indefinite. Do you not see that you would say: وامرأته الحمالة الحطب, so when you drop the alif and lām it is indefinite, and it is not proper to qualify a definite with an indefinite.
The other way is that you revile her for carrying firewood, so that her accusative is for blame (ʿalā al-dhamm), as was said: صلى الله عليه وسلم سيّد المرسلين, which al-Kisāʾī heard from the Arabs. [Translator's note: the sentence is apparently defective in the source; the example seems to illustrate the corresponding accusative of praise, «سيّدَ المرسلين».] We have mentioned [its like] in more than one place.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "وامرأته حمالةً للحطب", an indefinite in the accusative. She used to carry tales among people; that is her carrying firewood. He says: she stirred up strife among people and drew enmity between them.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فِى جِيدِهَا﴾: on her neck, ﴿حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍ﴾.
It is the chain that is in the Fire. And it is said: «من مسد»: it is the fibre of the doum palm (المُقْل).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «ما أغنى» is resumptive; «ما»: maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the maṣdar is conjoined to «ماله», i.e.: and his earning.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «وامرأته»: conjoined to the fāʿil (agent) in «يصلى», the conjunction being permitted by the separating element; «حمالة»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb (أذم) (I censure), and the clause (أذم) is parenthetical between the ḥāl (circumstantial) and the one it describes.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «في جيدها حبل» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «امرأته»; the preposition «مِنْ مسد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «حبل».

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying, Exalted is He (ما أغنى عنه ماله وما كسب): (ما) is in the position of the accusative by (أغنى); it is interrogative, a complete noun (ism tāmm). And it was said: (ما) is negation, and the object of (أغنى) is omitted, its implied form being «ما أغنى عنه ماله وكسبه شيئا» (his wealth and his earning availed him nothing).
His saying (وما كسب): (ما) is conjoined to (ماله). It has the meaning of (الذي), or together with the verb it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. «كسبه» (his earning). An omitted hāʾ must be implied if you make it mean (الذي), i.e. «كسبه» (what he earned).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (وامرأته حمالة الحطب): (امرأته) is conjoined to the latent pronoun in (سيصلى), and (حمالة) is nominative (marfūʿ) on the implication of «هي»: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). And it was said: (امرأته) is nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (حمالة) is its khabar. And it was said: the khabar is (في جيدها حبل), a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the khabar; likewise (حبل) may be made nominative by the [notion of] being settled (istiqrār), the clause being the khabar of (امرأته), and (حمالة) a naʿt (adjective) of the woman. If you make (حمالة) the khabar, His saying (في جيدها حبل) is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in (حمالة). Likewise, if you make (وامرأته حمالة) a mubtadaʾ and khabar, the clause may be in the position of a ḥāl from the hāʾ in (أغنى عنه). And it was said: (في جيدها حبل) is a second khabar of (امرأته).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿تبت﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the tāʾ is for the feminine.
﴿يدا﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the alif because it is a dual; the nūn was dropped for the construct, and it is muḍāf.
﴿أبي لهب﴾: أبي is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is one of the six nouns, and it is muḍāf; لهب is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿تبت﴾ is an imprecation (duʿāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.
﴿وتب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; تب is a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to ﴿أبي لهب﴾. The clause ﴿تب﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿تبت﴾ and has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ما﴾: interrogative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أغنى﴾, i.e. "What thing did wealth avail him?" Or ﴿ما﴾ is a negative particle with no grammatical position.
﴿أغنى﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa.
﴿عنه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أغنى﴾.
﴿ماله﴾: مال: the fāʿil (agent) of أغنى, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and it is muḍāf; the pronoun is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi. The clause ﴿ما أغنى عنه ماله﴾ is resumptive and has no grammatical position.
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun in the position of the nominative by conjunction to ﴿ماله﴾; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "and that which he earned". Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the nominative, conjoined to ﴿ماله﴾, i.e. "and his earning". Or ﴿ما﴾ is interrogative, in the position of the accusative as a fronted direct object of ﴿كسب﴾, i.e. "and what thing did he earn?" Or ﴿ما﴾ is a negative particle with no grammatical position, i.e. "he did not earn".
﴿كسب﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". The clause ﴿كسب﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position; on the view that ﴿ما﴾ is interrogative or negative, the clause ﴿ما كسب﴾ is conjoined to the one before it and has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿سيصلى﴾: the sīn is a particle of futurity; يصلى is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو", referring to ﴿أبي لهب﴾.
﴿نارا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿ذات﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نارا﴾, accusative by the fatḥa, and it is muḍāf.
﴿لهب﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وامرأته﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; امرأته is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿يصلى﴾, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿حمالة﴾: accusative (manṣūb) for censure (ʿalā al-dhamm) by an omitted verb, i.e. "I censure the carrier of firewood"; and حمالة is muḍāf.
﴿الحطب﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿في جيدها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun; جيد is muḍāf, and the pronoun is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi; the quasi-clause (shibh al-jumla) is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as a fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿حبل﴾: a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿من مسد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حبل﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: Concerning the first «تبّ» there are two views: one, that it is an imprecation (duʿāʾ); the other, that it is a statement of fact (khabar). Concerning the quiescence of the tāʾ there are two views: one, that since it is a particle, quiescence was necessary for it; the other, that no vowel remained for it, so it was kept still. يَدا: there are two views on it: one, that it is figurative (majāz), i.e., (he) perished; the other, that it is literal, as it is narrated that Abū Lahab wanted to throw (a stone) at the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prevented him from that, and revealed تبّت يدا أبي لهب, i.e., the two hands of Abū Lahab have perished. (أبي): there are two views on it: one, that the mark of the genitive is the yāʾ; and the other, that it is inflected from two sides — this is the view of the Kufans. وَتَبَّ: there are two views on it: one, that قد is implied in it, as it is narrated that Ibn Masʿūd read «تبّت يدا أبي لهب وقد تب»; and the other, that it is a statement of fact, and that «قد» is not implied, because it is a particle of meaning.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: ما أَغْنى عَنْهُ مالُهُ: concerning «ما» there are two views: one, that it is in the position of the accusative by أغنى; and the other, that it has no grammatical position and that it is negative. وَما كَسَبَ: there are two views on it: one, that what is meant by it is his child — this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās; and the other, whatever he earned of anything.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: There are two views on it: one, that the pause on it is ذاه with hāʾ, because the feminine of nouns is with hāʾ; and the other, that the pause is ذات, because it is not separated from what follows it in meaning.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
وَامْرَأَتُهُ: there are two views on it: one, that it is nominative because it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in سيصلى, the conjunction to the pronoun being good because of the length of the speech; and the other, that it is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ in the nominative [Translator's note: the printed vowelling shows the accusative; the nominative حَمَّالَةُ is meant here]: there are two views on it: one, that it is a naʿt (adjective) of امرأته; and the other, that it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. Concerning her being described with this there are two views — and she is Umm Jamīl [Translator's note: the text reads «أم جمل»], the sister of Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb: one of the two views is that she was described with this to debase her, as a punishment for her harming the Prophet ﷺ; and the other view is that he had wives other than her, so she was described with this to distinguish her from them. Concerning the position of the clause (فِي جِيدِها حَبْلٌ) there are two views: one, that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being "his wealth and what he earned did not avail him, and his wife, the carrier of firewood (with a rope on her neck)"; and the other, that it is the khabar of «ما» [Translator's note: so in the text], in the position of a ḥāl.
Whoever reads حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ (in the accusative): in his reading there are two views. One, that it is accusative as a ḥāl, because the alif-lām may enter it, so when you dropped them it was put in the accusative as a ḥāl [Translator's note: so in the text]. The other, that it is accusative by way of censure (dhamm), i.e., "I mean the carrier of firewood", as the poet said: [al-Rajaz] 590- نحن بني ضبّة أصحاب الجمل ("We — the Banū Ḍabba — the people of the Camel"); and Ruʾba said: [al-Rajaz] 591- أنا ابن سعد أكرم السّعدينا ("I am the son of Saʿd, the most noble of the Saʿds").

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: فِي جِيدِها: there are two views on it: one, that it is a khabar (predicate) after a khabar about «وامرأته»; and the other, that it is a khabar cut off from the first. حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ: there are two views on it: one, that what is meant by it is the chain that will be on her neck in the Fire; and the other, that it is the rope with which she used to carry the firewood.

safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) is negative [Note: or an interrogative noun, a fronted direct object.], (عنه) is attached to (أغنى), (ما) is a maṣdar particle..
and the interpreted maṣdar (ما كسب..) is in the position of nominative, conjoined to ماله.
Clause: «تبّت يدا ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «تبّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the inceptive clause.
And the clause: «ما أغنى عنه ماله ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «كسب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
3-5 (the sīn) is for futurity. (ذات) is an accusative naʿt of (نارا). (the wāw) is a conjunction – or resumptive –. (امرأته) is conjoined to the pronoun that is the agent in (يصلى) [Note: what made the conjunction permissible without mentioning the detached pronoun is the presence of the direct object.. and it is possible for (امرأته) to be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause في جيدها حبل.], (حمّالة) is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أذمّ" ("I censure") [Note: or a ḥāl from امرأته – al-ʿUkbarī allowed it –], (في جيدها) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (حبل), (من مسد) is attached to an adjective of (حبل)..
And the clause: «سيصلى ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «في جيدها حبل ... » has no grammatical position; it is another explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(أبو لهب): the kunya of ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, uncle of the Prophet ﷺ; he was so called because of the flaming redness of his face.
(حمّالة): the feminine of حمّال, an intensive form of the active participle from the triliteral حمل; its wazn is فعّالة.
(جيد): a non-derived noun meaning "neck"; its wazn is فعل with kasra then sukūn.
(مسد): a non-derived noun meaning "fibre"; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas. In al-Qāmūs: al-masad (with fatḥa on the sīn) is the iron axle, or a rope of fibre, or any tightly twisted rope; its plural is masād and amsād.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metaphor: in His saying, the Exalted: «وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ».
Of one who goes about with slander, it is said: he carries firewood among the people, i.e. he kindles distance between them and breeds evil; so firewood is borrowed for slander, and it is a well-known metaphor. Among it is the saying of the poet:
إن بني الادرم حمالو الحطب ... هم الوشاة في الرضاء والغضب
(The sons of al-Adram are carriers of firewood; they are the informers in contentment and in anger.)
2- The art of mockery (tahakkum): in His saying, the Exalted: «فِي جِيدِها حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ».
Here He depicted her in a picture of utmost baseness; the meaning is that she carries that bundle of thorns and ties it around her neck, as the woodcutters do, degrading her state and depicting her as one of the humble women woodcutters, so that she and her husband would be vexed by it, while they are in a house of honour and nobility.

* Benefits:
1- The style of ikhtiṣāṣ (specification) is a style in which an overt noun (that is, not a pronoun) is mentioned after the first-person pronoun, to make clear who is meant by it. This noun is called "al-mukhtaṣṣ".
2- The mukhtaṣṣ noun is made definite by (ال), as in: (نحن - العرب - نكرم الضيف), or by annexation, as in: (نحن - معاشر الأنبياء - لا نورث).
3- The mukhtaṣṣ is put in the accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being أخصّ or أعني, and the ikhtiṣāṣ clause is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.
4- The style of ikhtiṣāṣ may come with (أيّها or أيتها) followed by a noun made definite by (ال), as in: (أنا - أيها العبد - فقير إلى الله) (إنني - أيتها العجوز - أشكو ضعفي إلى الله). We parse (أيها or أيتها) as: a noun indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ, and (ها) is a particle of alerting; and the noun after it is parsed as a badal if it is non-derived, as in the first example, and as a ṣifa if it is derived, as in the example with (أيتها), the second example.
2- The inimitability of the Qur'an:
The scholars said: In this sūra is a miracle, which is that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has decisively and categorically stated that the destiny of Abū Lahab and his wife is the Fire, though it was possible and probable that Abū Lahab and his wife would enter Islam, as ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and other disbelievers entered it. But the persistence of Abū Lahab and his wife, and their dying in disbelief, is proof that the Qur'an is not the speech of a human being but is from the Knower of the unseen, who knows what man is and what he will become.
3- The occasion of revelation of the sūra:
On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When (وانذر عشيرتك الأقربين) was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ climbed al-Ṣafā and called: O sons of Fihr, O sons of ʿAdī – to the clans of Quraysh – until they gathered; and if a man could not come he sent a messenger. Abū Lahab and the Quraysh came, and he ﷺ said: Do you see that if I told you that horsemen in the valley wanted to raid you, would you believe me? They said: Yes, we have never experienced a lie from you. He said: Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment. Abū Lahab said: Ruin to you for the whole day! Is it for this that you gathered us? Then this sūra was revealed.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٍ}: i.e. they have lost. The explanation of this root was given in Sūrat Ghāfir at His saying: {إِلاَّ فِي تَبَابٍ} [Ghāfir: 37]. The verb was attributed to the two hands figuratively, because most acts are performed with them, even though the whole of the one cursed is meant. His saying «تَبَّتْ» is an imprecation (duʿāʾ), and «تَبَّ» is a statement, i.e. what was invoked against him has occurred; as in the poet's saying:
4668 - جَزاني جَزاه اللَّهُ شرَّ جَزائِه ... جزاءَ الكِلابِ العاوياتِ وقد فَعَلْ
(He repaid me — may Allah repay him the worst of repayment — with the repayment of howling dogs; and He has done so.)
This is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: «وقد تَبَّ». The apparent view is that both are imprecations; and in this there is something resembling the general coming after the specific, because the two hands are a part — even though the literal hands are not meant; He only expressed it with the two hands because acts are mostly performed with them.
The generality read «لَهَبٍ» with fatḥa on the hāʾ, and Ibn Kathīr with sukūn on it [«لَهْبٍ»]. It was said: they are two dialect forms with one meaning, like al-nahr and al-nahar, al-shaʿr and al-shaʿar, al-nafar and al-nafr, al-ḍajar and al-ḍajr. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a case of altering proper names, like his saying 'Shums ibn Mālik' with ḍamma" — meaning that the origin is Shams, with fatḥa on the shīn, which was altered to ḍamma; and he is alluding to the poet's saying:
4669 - وإنِّي لَمُهْدٍ مِنْ ثَنَائِي فَقاصِدٌ بِهِ ... لابنِ عَمِّ الصِّدْقِ شُمْسِ بنِ مالكِ
(I am presenting some of my praise, directing it to the true cousin, Shums ibn Mālik.)
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] allowed that «شُمْس» may be transferred from «شُمْس», the plural [of shamūs, restive], from the saying: "the tails of restive (shums) horses"; so it would not be a case of alteration at all. He was given this kunya either because of the flaming of his cheeks — he was bright-faced and ruddy — or because of what he will come to, the flame of Hell, as in their saying "Abū al-Khayr" and "Abū al-Sharr" because [good or evil] issue from them; or because the kunya is more prevalent than the name; or because it is lesser than it — hence He mentioned the prophets by their names, not their kunyas; or because of the ugliness of his name, for his name was "ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā", so He turned to the kunya. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why did He call him by his kunya, when the kunya is an honour?" — then he mentioned three answers: either because he was well known by his kunya, or because of the ugliness of his name as stated, or because his destination is the flame of Hell — end of quote. This implies that the kunya is nobler and more complete, not lesser, which is the opposite of a view stated just above.
It was read: «يدا أبو لَهَبٍ», with the wāw in the place of the genitive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As was said: ʿAlī ibn Abū Ṭālib and Muʿāwiya ibn Abū Sufyān, so that nothing in it is changed and it becomes confusing to the hearer. Flīta ibn Qāsim, the emir of Mecca, had two sons, one of them ʿAbdi-llāh with the genitive and the other ʿAbda-llāh with the accusative." The readers did not differ concerning His saying {ذاتَ لَهَب}: it is with fatḥa. The difference is that it is a verse-ending (fāṣila), and if it were made quiescent, the correspondence [of the verse-endings] would be lost.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {مَآ أغنى}: «ما» may be negative or interrogative. On the second it is in the position of the accusative by what follows it, the implied form being: "What did wealth avail?" It was placed first because it has the right to the beginning of the clause.
His saying: {وَمَا كَسَبَ}: «ما» here may be in the sense of «الذي», with the referring pronoun omitted; or maṣdariyya, i.e. "and his earning"; or interrogative, meaning: "and what did he earn?", i.e. he earned nothing — the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said this, making the interrogative mean negation. On this basis it may be negative, the meaning being as he mentioned; but this is not apparent. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read: «وما اكْتَسَبَ».

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {سيصلى}: the generality read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the ṣād and the lām without shadda, i.e. he himself will burn. Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Miqsam and ʿAbbās in his preferred reading (ikhtiyār) read with ḍamma, fatḥa and shadda [«سَيُصَلَّى»]. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read with ḍamma and sukūn [«سَيُصْلَى»].

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {وامرأته حَمَّالَةَ الحطب}: the reading of the generality is in the nominative, taking them as a clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) brought to state that. It was also said: «وامرأتُه» is conjoined to the pronoun in «سَيَصْلى», which is made permissible by the separation with the object. On this view there are several views about «حَمَّالةُ الحطبِ»: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «امرأتهُ» — that being permissible because the annexation is genuine (ḥaqīqiyya), since the past is meant; or that it is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); or that it is a badal (substitute), because it is close to non-derived nouns owing to the pure [definiteness of its] annexation; or that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "she is the carrier". Ibn ʿAbbās read «ومُرَيَّتُهُ» and «ومُرَيْئَتُهُ» in the diminutive, except that he kept the hamza at one time, and at another changed it into yāʾ and assimilated [the yāʾ] into it.
The generality read {حَمَّالَةُ} in the nominative, and ʿĀṣim in the accusative. It was said: by way of reviling (shatm); "he did a fine thing (jamīl) who reviled Umm Jamīl" — al-Zamakhsharī said this; she was known by the kunya Umm Jamīl. It was also said: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «امرأتُه», if we make it nominative by conjunction to the pronoun. Making it a ḥāl from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase after it, if we make that the khabar of «امرأتُه», is weak according to the majority, because it precedes its abstract governor (al-ʿāmil al-maʿnawī). Some found the ḥāl reading problematic because of what was said before, that the past is meant by it, so it becomes definite through the annexation; so how can it be a ḥāl according to the majority? Then he answered that the future is meant, because it is reported in the exegesis that she will carry on the Day of Resurrection a bundle of the firewood of the Fire, as she used to carry firewood in this world.
Concerning His saying {حَمَّالَةَ الحطب} there are two views. The first: it is literal. The second: it is a figure for going about with slander and sowing discord among people. The poet said:
4670 - إنَّ بني الأَدْرَمِ حَمَّالو الحَطَبْ ... هُمُ الوشاةُ في الرِّضا وفي الغضبْ
(The Banū al-Adram are carriers of firewood: they are the slanderers in content and in anger.)
Another said:
4671 - مِنْ البِيْضِ لم تُصْطَدْ على ظَهْرِ لأْمَةٍ ... ولم تَمْشِ بين الحَيِِّ بالحطبِ الرَّطْبِ
(One of the fair women, not caught upon a disgrace, and who does not go about among the clan with fresh firewood.)
He made it fresh to point to its smoking, and this is close to reinforcing the metaphor (tarshīḥ al-majāz). Abū Qilāba read {حاملةَ الحطبِ} on the pattern fāʿila; it admits [the same senses as] the reading of the generality. ʿAbbās read «حَمَّالةٌ للحطَبِ» with tanwīn and the object made genitive by a redundant (zāʾida) lām strengthening the governor, as in His saying, exalted is He: {فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ} [Hūd: 107]. Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read «وامرأتُه» with the hāʾ snatched (ikhtilās), without full lengthening.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ}: «في جيدِها» may be the khabar (predicate) of «امرأتُه», with «حبلٌ» as its fāʿil (agent); or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «امرأتُه» on the view that it is an agent [conjoined to the pronoun], with «حبلٌ» likewise nominative by it; or a fronted khabar with «حَبْلٌ» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being a ḥāl or a second khabar. Al-jīd: the neck; its plural is ajyād. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4672 - وجِيْدٍ كجِيْدِ الرِّئْمِ ليس بفاحِشٍ ... إذا هي نَصَّتْهُ ولا بمُعْطَّلِ
(And a neck like the neck of a white antelope, not ungainly when she raises it, nor bare of ornament.)
{مِّن مَّسَدٍ} is an adjective of «حَبْل». Al-masad: the fibre of the doum palm; it was also said: fibre in general; and it was said: it is the bark of a tree in Yemen. Al-Nābigha said:
4673 - مَقْذُوْفَةٌ بِدَخِيْسِ النَّحْضِ بَازِلُها ... له صريفٌ صَريفُ القَعْوِ بالمَسَدِ
(Pelted with compact flesh, her tusk grinds with a creak like the creak of a pulley-wheel on a palm-fibre rope.)
It may also be of camels' hides and hair; he recited:
4647 - ومَسَدٍ أُمِرَّ مِنْ أَيانِقِ ...
(And a rope twisted firmly from [the hides of] young she-camels…)
[Translator's note: the verse number appears thus (4647) in the source; by sequence 4674 would be expected.]
One says: "a man mamsūd of build", i.e. strong of it.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ (١)).
The words of the Exalted (أَبِي لَهَبٍ): it is read with a fatḥa on the hāʾ and with sukūn; they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ (٢)).
The words of the Exalted (مَا أَغْنَى): it may be a negation, and it may be an interrogative; it cannot be in the sense of «الَّذِي» (that which).

ukberi-tibyan:4-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ (٤) فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ (٥)).
The words of the Exalted (وَامْرَأَتُهُ): there are two views on it. The first: it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the pronoun in «يَصْلَى»; on this view there are two views on «حَمَّالَةَ»:
The first: it is a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes it. The second: its implied form is «هِيَ حَمَّالَةُ» (she is the carrier). «فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «حَمَّالَةَ». (حَمَّالَةَ) is read in the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. she will burn in the Fire with that being said to her; but the better (al-jayyid) is that it be accusative as a term of censure (ʿalā al-dhamm), i.e. «أَذُمُّ» (I censure) or «أَعْنِي» (I mean). The other view: that «امْرَأَتُهُ» is a mubtadaʾ and «حَمَّالَةُ» its khabar, and «فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «حَمَّالَة», or a second khabar.
It is also possible for «حَبْلٌ» to be put in the nominative by the adverbial phrase (ẓarf), because it is supported [by what precedes it]; and whoever reads «حَمَّالَةَ» in the accusative makes the clause after it the khabar.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat ”تَبَّتْ“ (Tabbat)
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدا أبِي لَهَبٍ وتَبَّ﴾ ("perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he"): its meaning is: "the hands of Abū Lahab have lost", and ”وَتَبَّ“, that is: and he has lost. It has come in the exegesis «that the Prophet ﷺ invited his uncles and set before them a bowl of food. They said: "One of us alone eats a whole sheep, and he has set before us only this bowl!" Then they all ate from it, and nothing but a small amount was diminished from it. They said: "What will we have with you if we follow you?" He said: ”لَكم ما لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ، وعَلَيْكم ما عَلَيْهِمْ، وإنَّما تَتَفاضَلُونَ في الدِّينِ“ ("You will have what the Muslims have, and owe what they owe; you will excel one another only in religion"). Abū Lahab said: "Perish you! Is it for this that you invited us?!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدا أبِي لَهَبٍ وتَبَّ﴾».

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying: ﴿ما أغْنى عَنْهُ مالُهُ وما كَسَبَ﴾ ("his wealth and what he earned will not avail him"): the exegetes said: ”ما كَسَبَ“ here is his children. The position of ”ما“ is nominative (rafʿ); the meaning is: "his wealth and his earning did not avail him".

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿سَيَصْلى نارًا ذاتَ لَهَبٍ﴾ ("he will roast in a Fire of flame"): that is, and his children will roast in a Fire of flame. It is also read: ”سَيُصْلى نارًا“ (passive: "he will be made to roast in a Fire").

zajjaj:4-4.t:
”وامْرَأتُهُ حَمّالَةُ الحَطَبِ“ ("and his wife, the carrier of firewood", nominative); it is also read ﴿حَمّالَةَ الحَطَبِ﴾ in the accusative. ”اِمْرَأتُهُ“ is nominative on two grounds. One of them is conjunction (ʿaṭf) with what is [latent] in ”سَيَصْلى“; the meaning is "he will roast, he and his wife", and ”حَمّالَةُ الحَطَبِ“ is then a naʿt (adjective) of her. Whoever reads it in the accusative does so as [an accusative of] censure (ʿalā al-dhamm), the meaning being "I mean the carrier of firewood". And ﴿وامْرَأتُهُ﴾ may be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with ”حَمّالَةُ“ part of its description, and the khabar (predicate) being ﴿فِي جِيدِها حَبْلٌ مِن مَسَدٍ﴾ [al-Masad: 5] ("around her neck is a rope of palm fibre"), as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
And it has come in the exegesis about ﴿حَمّالَةَ الحَطَبِ﴾ that she was Umm Jamīl, and that she used to go about with slander. The poet said:
مِنَ البِيضِ لَمْ تُصْطَدْ عَلى ظَهْرِ لَأْمَةٍ ∗∗∗ ولَمْ تَمْشِ بَيْنَ الحَيِّ بِالحَطَبِ الرَّطْبِ
(One of the fair women, not caught out in any blameworthy act, who has not gone about among the tribe with fresh firewood.)
That is: with slander. And it was said: she used to carry thorns, the thorns of the ʿiḍāh shrub, and throw them in the path of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِي جِيدِها حَبْلٌ مِن مَسَدٍ﴾ ("around her neck is a rope of masad"): ”اَلْجِيدُ“ is the neck. And it was said in the exegesis: ﴿حَبْلٌ مِن مَسَدٍ﴾ is a chain seventy cubits long, meaning that she will be threaded into the chain seventy cubits. And ”اَلْمَسَدُ“ in the language of the Arabs is a rope when it is made of the fibre of the doum palm (al-muql); and ropes made from the [hair of the] backs of camels may also be called ”مَسَدٌ“. The poet said:
وَمَسَدٍ أُمِرَّ مِن أيانُقِ
(And a masad rope twisted firm from [the hair of] she-camels.)
